content: 1. The interaction between alvimopan and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter may lead to an increased level or effect of alvimopan. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown and considered minor. 2. Indinavir can increase the level or effect of ambrisentan by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. This interaction is minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is advised. 3. Indinavir may elevate the level or effect of amikacin through its interaction with the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is recommended, and close monitoring is necessary. 4. Amiodarone increases the level or effect of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is contraindicated due to its serious nature, and alternative therapies should be considered. 5. Indinavir can enhance the level or effect of amiodarone by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used to avoid potential adverse effects. 6. Indinavir increases the level or effect of amitriptyline via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. 7. Amobarbital decreases the level or effect of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is necessary, and close monitoring is recommended. 8. Anastrozole may increase the level or effect of indinavir by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 9. Indinavir increases the level or effect of apalutamide by influencing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 10. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers can lower the exposure to CYP3A4 substrates, potentially reducing their therapeutic effect. 11. Indinavir increases the level or effect of apixaban by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. 12. Aprepitant increases the level or effect of indinavir by influencing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Similarly, indinavir increases the level or effect of aprepitant. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 13. Indinavir increases the level or effect of aripiprazole by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is recommended, and close monitoring is required. 14. Armodafinil decreases the level or effect of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Conversely, indinavir increases the level or effect of armodafinil through both CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the level or effect of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Indinavir, in turn, increases the level or effect of artemether/lumefantrine. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 16. Atazanavir increases the level or effect of indinavir by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 17. Indinavir increases the level or effect of atogepant by influencing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. The atogepant dosage should be reduced to 10 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 18. Atorvastatin levels and toxicity are increased by indinavir through CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. The risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis is heightened when atorvastatin is co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Indinavir decreases the level or effect of atovaquone through an unknown mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 20. Indinavir increases the level or effect of avanafil by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. This interaction is serious, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse events such as hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. 21. Indinavir increases the level or effect of avapritinib by influencing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. 22. Indinavir increases the level or effect of axitinib by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, the axitinib dose should be reduced by 50%. 23. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of indinavir through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. 24. Indinavir increases the level or effect of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by affecting both CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is recommended, and close monitoring is necessary. 25. Indinavir increases the level or effect of bedaquiline by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days should be avoided unless the benefits outweigh the risks. 26. Indinavir increases the level or effect of belinostat by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration with strong UGT inhibitors requires a reduced belinostat starting dose of 750 mg/m². Close monitoring is necessary. 27. Belzutifan decreases the level or effect of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 28. Indinavir increases the level or effect of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may lead to potentially fatal respiratory depression. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 29. Indinavir increases the level or effect of bortezomib by influencing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 30. Bosentan decreases the level or effect of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 31. Indinavir increases the level or effect of bosutinib by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases bosutinib plasma concentration approximately fivefold. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 32. Indinavir increases the level or effect of brentuximab vedotin by influencing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Patients should be monitored for adverse reactions. 33. Indinavir increases the level or effect of brexpiprazole by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. The brexpiprazole dose should be halved when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor is also used, the dose should be reduced to a quarter. 34. Indinavir increases the level or effect of brigatinib by influencing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be avoided, the brigatinib dose should be reduced by 50%. 35. Indinavir increases the level or effect of bromocriptine by decreasing its metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 36. Indinavir increases the level or effect of budesonide by affecting both CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 37. Indinavir increases the level or effect of buprenorphine (including buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection forms) by influencing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required due to the potential for increased toxicity. 38. Indinavir increases the level or effect of buspirone by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is recommended, and close monitoring is necessary. 39. Butabarbital and butalbital decrease the level or effect of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. 40. Indinavir increases the level or effect of cabazitaxel by influencing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary due to the potential for increased toxicity. 41. Indinavir increases the level or effect of cabergoline by decreasing its metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 42. Indinavir increases the level or effect of cabozantinib by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided. If required, the cabozantinib dose should be reduced accordingly. 43. Indinavir increases the level or effect of calcifediol by affecting CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary, as this interaction may alter vitamin D metabolism. 44. Indinavir increases the level or effect of calcitriol by influencing CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 45. Calcium carbonate decreases the level or effect of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral form of indinavir.
